topIssues.title: [Epic] Ship the agentic parent suite with trustworthy household coordination
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Goal

Ship a trustworthy LifeOps parent-assistant suite that materially reduces the
anticipation, planning, coordination, monitoring, and recovery work carried by
a busy world-traveling mother coordinating children with a co-parent and
caregivers.

The completed system must ingest authoritative household sources, reason over
multiple calendars without leaking private event details, distinguish proposals
from agreements, obtain the right approvals, monitor material changes, execute
typed transactions exactly once, and verify closure. It must expose source
freshness and errors instead of presenting unavailable data as a healthy empty
state.

## Design doc

`packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/11-agentic-parent-suite.md`

## Scope

- Calendar source registry, sync health, multi-account aggregation, guest
  free/busy, ICS/webcal, and Microsoft Graph calendar support.
- Deterministic conflict/availability evaluation for time, people, custody,
  caregivers, transport, locations, resources, travel, recurrence, time zones,
  DST, and all-day events.
- Typed schedule proposals, per-party agreements, material-change
  invalidation, approval-gated messaging, and provider materialization.
- Household roles, scoped/expiring caregiver access, private-busy projection,
  append-only audit, and scoped export.
- School/activity ingestion and correction monitoring; action bundles,
  responsibility ownership, seasonal opportunities, household items, and
  external-source adapters.
- Food constraints, inventory confidence, cart/order idempotency, delivery
  exception recovery, childcare/work modeling, and source-grounded parenting
  guidance with human handoff.
- A composite world-traveling co-parent persona plus G1-G48 capability
  scenarios, real-provider tests, live-model trajectories, and manually
  reviewed evidence.

## Non-goals

- A second scheduler, household graph, connector abstraction, or file store.
- Behavior keyed from prompt text or demographic runtime modes.
- Autonomous sensitive messages, custody changes, medical/legal decisions, or
  purchases without typed policy and required approval.
- Scraping private guest calendars or fabricating availability, inventory,
  costs, source health, transactions, or completion.

## Work Items

- [ ] Ratify calendar-source health, proposal/agreement, access, audit,
      responsibility, provenance, and transaction contracts.
- [ ] Consolidate conflict detection and wire production guest free/busy.
- [ ] Route scheduling lifecycle communication through draft and approval
      policy.
- [ ] Implement provider-neutral sync, pagination, cursors, webhooks, and
      idempotent reconciliation.
- [ ] Implement Microsoft and hardened ICS/webcal sources.
- [ ] Implement household roles, scoped access, private-busy, audit, and export.
- [ ] Implement schedule proposals, approvals, materiality, and final
      calendar materialization.
- [ ] Implement school/activity ingestion, correction monitoring, action
      bundles, and weekly responsibility review.
- [ ] Implement weather/maps/local-activity sources and seasonal/household
      item workflows.
- [ ] Implement food, inventory, cart, order, refund, and delivery-recovery
      workflows.
- [ ] Implement deterministic childcare/work scenarios and source-grounded
      parenting guidance boundaries.
- [ ] Author and live-verify G1-G48 plus all ten Jordan co-parent scenarios.
- [ ] Reconcile every overlapping open LifeOps issue and PR; reuse valid work
      and close no item until the production path and evidence are complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every row in the design doc delivery ledger is complete.
- [ ] The busy world-traveling co-parent journey works from source ingestion
      through conflict discovery, privacy-preserving coordination, approval,
      materialization, change recovery, and closure.
- [ ] Loading, designed-empty, unavailable, stale, partial, and error states are
      distinguishable at every source boundary.
- [ ] No private event title, child-private fact, or unrelated adult data leaks
      across household scopes or exports.
- [ ] Duplicate/out-of-order provider events, retries, concurrent approvals,
      recurrence edits, DST/date-line crossings, and transaction retries are
      deterministic and idempotent.
- [ ] Real-provider or sandbox-provider contracts cover every connector; mocks
      and deterministic LLM fixtures are supplemental only.
- [ ] Live-model scenarios record inputs, provider context, actions, outputs,
      and domain artifacts, and every artifact is manually reviewed.
- [ ] Full package tests, repository verification, and all applicable UI,
      security, and evidence gates pass after rebasing on `origin/develop`.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: full desktop/mobile flow where UI applies;
      otherwise an explicit N/A reason per backend-only work item.
- [ ] Logs: structured backend logs plus frontend console/network logs where UI
      applies, including success, partial-source, stale, permission, and recovery
      paths.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: JSON report, run viewer, and native JSONL for the
      persona and adversarial corpus, opened and reviewed by hand.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: calendar events/provider IDs, approvals, proposals,
      access grants, audit events/exports, source versions, scheduled tasks,
      carts/orders/receipts/refunds, and completion records.
- [ ] CI runs: scoped package lanes, full `bun run verify`, relevant real E2E
      lanes, and all PR checks.

## Dependencies / Sequencing

- Project: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/15>
- Coordination: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14407>
- Persona and journey workstream: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14392>
- Process and evidence workstream: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14406>
- Existing co-parent E2E: #14789
- Relationship inference/capture: #14785 and #14786
- Scheduling output proof: #14874
- Multi-account source ingestion: #14758 and #14792
- Existing LifeOps live verification: #16938 and #16941
- Side-effect receipts and final send-boundary proof: #17027

Sequence the truth and authorization layers before new convenience domains:
calendar/source health → proposals/access/audit → school/household sources →
food/transactions → financial/guidance surfaces → complete live persona proof.

topIssues.title: fix(cloud): correlate preserved canary deletion errors with bounded history
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Problem

The post-merge read-only staging diagnostic run 30231515082 stopped fail-closed at the preserved sandbox error boundary after the bounded delete-job history had sanitized successfully. The sandbox writer stores a canonical permanent-delete wrapper, while recovery re-enqueue preserves that wrapper as newer delete jobs are added. Coarse error-code equality is insufficient for an unclassified cause and the raw value must never leave the runner.

Parent lifecycle investigation: #17184. Previous bounded-history fix: #17198.

## Scope

- Parse exactly one canonical permanent-delete wrapper and bind its attempt count.
- Correlate the raw cause only in memory to an exact exhausted failed job within the already bounded newest-three history.
- Reuse that job sanitized classification/profile; emit no raw value, hash, source index, or new sandbox profile.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior for unmatched, ambiguous, nested, malformed, direct opaque, result-error, lifecycle, counter, and ordering boundaries.
- Preserve schema v3 and the read-only workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- Exact cause + attempts + terminal lifecycle correlation is required.
- deletion_failed binds the latest job; deletion_pending may bind an older retained failure after recovery re-enqueue.
- Deletion ownership and a positive persisted failure count are required for the canonical wrapper.
- Adversarial tests cover cause/counter/status/order mismatch, wrapper lookalikes/nesting, all three bounded positions, same-shape secret variants, and forbidden-output scanning.
- Focused tests, Biome, diff check, full verify, and independent exact-object review pass.
- A new read-only diagnostic is not dispatched until the merged source is exact and separately authorized; no delete retry, manual database write, global pin, or staging mutation is part of this issue.

## Evidence

- Backend logs: N/A - the public workflow annotation identifies only the classifier boundary and exposes no raw value.
- Frontend logs: N/A - backend workflow-only change.
- Screenshots: N/A - no user interface change.
- Video: N/A - no user interface change.
- Real-model trajectory: N/A - no model behavior change.
- Domain artifact: N/A - the prior run intentionally uploaded no artifact after fail-closed classification.

topIssues.title: P0: agent deletion is failing 100% in production (160/160 jobs, 37 agents stuck) + 78% overall job failure rate
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Summary

A live production audit of the provisioning pipeline (2026-07-29) found **agent deletion is failing 100% of the time**, and has been for days. This is customer-visible and accelerating.

Over the last 7 days: **554 failed jobs vs 153 completed** (78% failure rate).

## 1. `agent_delete` is completely broken — 160/160 failures, one identical cause

Every failed `agent_delete` job in the window carries the same error:

```
value.toISOString is not a function
```

- 160 failures, all identical, most recent **2026-07-28 18:03 UTC** (still current).
- All of them exhausted `attempts >= max_attempts` — so each one also burned the full retry budget.
- Consequence: **37 agents are stuck in `deletion_failed`**, up from 5 five days ago, and accelerating: **17 of them in the last 24 hours alone**.
- Customers who ask to delete an agent get a failure, the agent stays, and it keeps occupying node capacity.

`value.toISOString is not a function` is Drizzle's timestamp serializer receiving a **string where a `Date` is expected** — the same class as the cache/JSON round-trip defect fixed in #16859/#16860 for `resolveSharedAgent`.

One concrete candidate worth checking first (not yet proven to be the site): `prepareAgentBackupInsertData` (`packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/agent-sandboxes.ts`) does

```ts
const createdAt = data.created_at ?? new Date();
// ...
created_at: createdAt,
```

`??` only guards `null`/`undefined` — a value that already crossed a JSON boundary as an ISO **string** passes straight through into the timestamp column. The 4 non-restart `agent_snapshot` failures in the same window are literally `Failed query: insert into "agent_sandbox_backups" (...)`, which is that insert.

## 2. `agent_snapshot`: 386 failures, 381 of them not the job's fault

```
Job interrupted by worker restart 2 times - max attempts reached   (381)
Failed query: insert into "agent_sandbox_backups" ...              (4)
Job timed out 2 times - max attempts reached                       (1)
```

The worker keeps restarting mid-snapshot, and **each restart consumes an attempt**. Two restarts exhaust `max_attempts` and the job is marked permanently failed — even though nothing about the job itself failed. A restart is an infrastructure event, not a job defect, and should not spend the job's retry budget (the codebase already has the shape for this: `retryLaterWithoutIncrementingAttempts`).

Why the worker restarts so often is the second half of this: it is consistent with the heap abort in #17154 and with the unbounded source-side snapshot capture in #17172 §1 (a large agent's capture is materialized entirely in the worker's heap).

## 3. The fleet is at or over capacity

| node | capacity | running |
|---|---|---|
| eliza-core-prod-2 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-3 | 24 | **25** |
| eliza-core-prod-4 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-5 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-6 | 24 | 24 |

prod-3 is **over** its declared capacity, and every robot is full, so new work is spilling onto autoscaled cloud nodes (3 × 4 running). Note the interaction: the 37 undeletable agents and the 45 in `error` are holding slots that should have been reclaimed — the delete failure is directly feeding the capacity pressure.

Also present: a `knowledge_processing` job stuck `in_progress` since **2025-12-31** (~7 months), which no sweeper has reclaimed.

## Why these compound

The three interact rather than being independent:
1. Deletes fail → agents accumulate (`deletion_failed` 37, `error` 45) → capacity fills.
2. Snapshots fail on worker restart → upgrades/deletes that depend on a restore point are less safe.
3. Full capacity → more scheduling pressure → longer boots → more exposure to the sweeper/timeout classes (#17215).

## Asks

- [ ] Pin and fix the `toISOString` write in the delete path — deterministic, 100% reproducible, highest customer impact.
- [ ] A worker restart must not consume a job's retry budget (`retryLaterWithoutIncrementingAttempts` semantics for interruption).
- [ ] Recover the 37 `deletion_failed` + 45 `error` rows once the above land (see #17162 for the 44-agent precedent and its recovery constraints).
- [ ] Reconcile declared capacity vs actual (prod-3 at 25/24), and reclaim the 7-month-stuck `in_progress` job.

Evidence gathered live against production (counts, error strings, timings; no customer identifiers). Related: #17215 (sweeper vs in-flight cold boots), #17154 (worker heap abort), #17172 (snapshot budgets), #17162 (the 2026-07-13 stranding), #17185 (delete must release capacity exactly once). [stan-cloud]

# Relates to

Relates to #17175, #17176, #17177, #17178, #17179, and #17181.

The research, architecture, capability ledger, connector plan, persona,
48-scenario corpus, implementation phases, and evidence status are documented
in
[`packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/11-agentic-parent-suite.md`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/feat/agentic-parent-suite/packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/11-agentic-parent-suite.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest
      `origin/develop` with zero conflicts (`8132bc67366`).
- [x] `bun install` and `bun run verify` were run after sync.
- [ ] A reviewer can confirm the complete live-provider product journey without
      reading the code. This remains a draft because live OAuth/webhook/provider
      proof is incomplete and G1 correctly failed.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased onto the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun run verify` passes post-sync.

# Risks

**Large.** This is a broad foundation PR (297 files) spanning calendar source
identity, availability, recurrence/timezone behavior, native Apple permission
semantics, Google watch lifecycle, immutable approval and mutation receipts,
household resource capacity, personal-assistant domains, one shared scheduler,
connector contracts, UI, benchmark provenance, and a SQL migration.

Primary risks are incorrect authority or tenant binding, duplicated external
effects during retry, recurrence/DST mistakes, stale source truth, webhook
abuse, accidental data disclosure across households/calendars, native
permission-mode drift, and UI states that hide a partial provider failure. The
new paths fail closed, use source/tenant/version/idempotency bindings, and have
focused real-PGlite and contract coverage; live providers remain a draft gate.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds the full world-traveling co-parent persona and G1-G48 test catalog, plus
  a 12,792-word implementation report grounded in 31 official, research,
  safety, and first-person sources.
- Adds source-aware calendar availability across selected Google, Apple,
  Microsoft, and ICS feeds, including health/freshness/provenance and explicit
  partial/error states.
- Adds durable Google push-channel bindings, strict notification validation,
  dedupe/order checks, scheduled retries and renewals, restart reconstruction,
  quota classification, and controlled 410 resync.
- Adds immutable calendar mutation proposals, exact owner/editor routing,
  approval CAS, replay receipts, series/version/tenant/source binding, Apple
  add-only semantics, and truthful invitation decline behavior.
- Adds deterministic caregiver/vehicle/restraint capacity solving with
  authorization, accessibility, freshness, handoff, transition,
  distinct-resource, invalidation, and shared-review constraints.
- Extends one shared `ScheduledTask` architecture and typed dispatch results; it
  does not add a second scheduler.
- Adds school-source reconciliation, household operations, family
  communications, food/inventory, parenting guidance,
  weather/routes/activity oracle, and childcare/work-scenario foundations with
  explicit source and safety contracts.
- Adds a calendar source manager UI and native permission presentation, plus
  desktop/mobile screenshots and a walkthrough harness.
- Fixes LifeOpsBench acting-agent provenance so adapter/provider/model are
  distinct from evaluator/judge identity and incomplete artifacts are rejected.

## What kind of change is this?

Features, improvements, tests, documentation, and one additive database
migration.

# Documentation changes needed?

- [x] Documentation is required and included.
- [x] The MVP persona documentation and ongoing-development index are updated.
- [x] The detailed report records what exists, what is missing, which work
      belongs to the LLM, which pieces require deterministic
      primitives/connectors, human failure modes, implementation phases,
      G1-G48 scenarios, and the exact evidence contract.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

1. Read the executive status and capability ledger in the report linked above.
2. Inspect the calendar source manager screenshots/video and the real G1
   failure trajectory in the evidence rows.
3. Review the durable Google watch test, owner calendar mutation gateway
   integration test, and resource-capacity PGlite integration test.
4. Confirm the report's explicit `0/48 complete` statement before interpreting
   the implementation status.

## Detailed testing completed

- `bun install` completed in the clean rebased worktree, including the required
  971 MiB artifact sync.
- `bun run verify`: **578/578 successful Turbo tasks** across 254 packages;
  lint, build, typecheck, dependency/script audits, 8,661-test-file anti-focus
  scan, and 28 dist-path consumer checks passed.
- Complete personal-assistant suite: **1,629 passed in 204 files, 8 intentional
  skips**, followed by a clean package TypeScript check.
- Calendar connector/service suite: **348 passed, 2 intentional live-provider
  skips**; Google connector suite 38 passed; connector shim 30 passed;
  public-route audit 5 passed.
- Source manager: 60 component/hook assertions and 63 focused
  accessibility/visual checks passed; five rendered iterations were reviewed.
- Immutable calendar mutation and owner-editor paths: 31 real-PGlite
  integration cases; EventEditor/routes/client contracts: 35 cases.
- Native Apple seam: 7 cases; Swift bridge contract: 15 cases.
- Household resource capacity: 15 real-PGlite cases; owner/affected-party
  resolution: 20 cases.
- LifeOpsBench changed-area regressions: 62 passed under Python 3.12.
- Focused evidence rerun: Google watch 8 passed; owner mutation gateway 13
  passed; resource capacity 15 passed.
- App audit: 252 views, 218 good, 25 manual-review, 9 pre-existing unrelated
  `needs-work`, 0 broken. Calendar desktop was good; three smaller calendar
  viewports were manually reviewed with no reported
  quality/console/overflow/color/hover defect.
- iOS cloud simulator build/install/launch succeeded. A real EventKit
  transaction was not possible without a reachable authenticated cloud
  backend.
- Real G1 model run: 12 turns with an acting-agent/evaluator/judge provenance
  chain and workload hash. It scored 0.0 and was manually reviewed. It repeated
  generic calendar searches, lacked a source-connect action, invented contact
  details, attempted an unapproved write, and then duplicated it. This is useful
  failure evidence, not a passing journey.

# Evidence Gate

<!-- evidence-row:before-screenshots -->
- [x] ![before-screenshots](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-before.jpg)
<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- [x] ![after-screenshots](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-after.jpg)
<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- [x] https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-walkthrough.mp4
<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->
- [x] [17206-backend-domain-tests.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-backend-domain-tests.log)
<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->
- [x] [17206-app-audit-report.json](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-app-audit-report.json)
<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->
- [x] [17206-g1-live-failure-trajectory.json](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-g1-live-failure-trajectory.json)
<!-- evidence-row:domain-artifacts -->
- [x] [17206-verify.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-verify.log)
<!-- evidence-row:ocr-review -->
- [x] [17206-calendar-source-ocr-review.json](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-ocr-review.json)

# Evidence Details

The evidence rows will contain JPG desktop/mobile before and after comparisons,
MP4 source-manager walkthrough, real-PGlite backend logs, the full app audit
report, OCR review, the provenance-valid G1 live trajectory, the clean
repository verification log, and iOS build/install/launch proof. Every artifact
was manually inspected and secret-scanned before upload.

## Known gaps / failures

- **0 of G1-G48 currently satisfies the complete live evidence contract.** The
  report says this explicitly and lists the missing proof per scenario family.
- The most important newly observed product gap is an agent-facing typed source
  list/select/connect/reconnect action. Owner UI/routes exist, but the acting
  agent could not invoke them in G1.
- Live multi-account Google/Microsoft OAuth, shared/guest grant acquisition,
  Apple EventKit mutation, uniquely routed public Google webhook delivery,
  provider WAF/rate-limit proof, and real-provider receipt review remain
  pending.
- Raw school inbox/document/photo/portal ingestion, real maps/travel-time
  composition, production grocery inventory/purchase, authenticated family
  messaging/reply, and acoustic speaker identity remain incomplete.
- The global app audit is not represented as clean: it passed 253 Playwright
  checks but its ratchet remains red because of nine unrelated pre-existing
  views.
- The iOS evidence proves the exact branch built, installed, and launched; it
  does not prove EventKit execution because no authenticated cloud backend was
  reachable.
- The real G1 trajectory is a failed run and must not be treated as qualifying
  success evidence.
- The exhaustive Python benchmark suite was not completed; the 62 directly
  affected Python 3.12 regressions passed. The full TypeScript
  personal-assistant suite and repository-wide verify both completed.

This PR stays draft until reviewers decide whether to split the broad foundation
or continue adding live-provider evidence on this branch.

topPRs.title: Fix/skunkscan funding token transfer wiring
topPRs.author: SkunkscanAI
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- `analyzers/funding.ts` now falls back to the first incoming SPL token transfer for
  initial-funding-source detection when no native SOL transfer is found, and tags the
  result as native/token/unknown via a new `fundingTransferType` field.
- Fixed a pre-existing wiring bug in `pipeline/walletPipeline.ts`: `analyzeWalletFunding`
  was receiving the raw Helius `SolanaParsedTransaction` (fields `fromUserAccount`/
  `toUserAccount`/`amount`) where it expects the normalized `ParsedWalletTransaction`
  (`from`/`to`/`amountSol`/`tokenTransfers`). `parseSolanaTransaction()` existed in
  `parsers/transaction.ts` but was never called anywhere, so this analyzer's
  native-transfer detection silently never matched at runtime.

## Evidence (PR_EVIDENCE.md)
- **Real LLM-call trajectory**: N/A — no agent/action/prompt/model behavior involved.
- **Backend/frontend logs**: N/A — pure data-transformation analyzer, no live service to log.
- **Screenshots/video**: N/A — no UI surface.
- **Type-check diff (before/after)**: Ran `bun run --cwd packages/agent typecheck`,
  stashing these 4 files out for a baseline (102 pre-existing errors) vs. restored
  (101 errors). The only change is the disappearance of the exact wiring-bug error
  this PR fixes (`walletPipeline.ts` SolanaParsedTransaction→ParsedWalletTransaction
  mismatch); zero new errors introduced by these 4 files.
- No existing tests cover this analyzer (`packages/agent/src/skunkscan` has no test
  files at all), so no test suite evidence to attach.

## Test plan
- [ ] `bun run --cwd packages/agent typecheck` (still has 101 pre-existing unrelated errors, none new)
- [ ] Manual review of `analyzers/funding.ts` branch logic

topPRs.title: fix(app): harden Android device evidence and deep-link delivery
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Relates to #13580 and #13581. This closes the agent-resolvable hosted-emulator and evidence-delivery residuals. The arm64 LOCAL round trip remains open until a runner with labels `self-hosted`, `linux`, `ARM64`, `android-device` is provisioned.

Definition of Done: full standard in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

- [x] Targets `develop`; exact head `e44bd654f26` is based on current `origin/develop` (`0f8045c6744d6dd696a57ba0a053f9f2ee55355c`).
- [x] Focused real-path tests, changed-file coverage, Android compilation, and `bun run verify` pass.
- [x] The exact-head mandatory app audit passed 246/246 views with no broken or needs-work verdicts.
- [ ] The exact-head API-34 PR/device and full-hosted emulator runs are in progress; every resulting artifact will be opened before the draft is promoted.

# What this fixes

The Android lane had several independent false-proof paths:

- `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` executes each nonblank script line in a separate `sh -c`, so multiline Bash state, traps, PIDs, continuations, and `pipefail` were lost;
- a cold native `appUrlOpen` could arrive while the startup splash listener was mounted but still restoring reset/session state; reading `gatewayUrl` falsely acknowledged the command immediately before restore cleared the newly selected remote;
- hosted emulators expose a hardware keyboard, suppressing the real software IME even after the probe requested it, and the verifier sampled UIAutomator only once;
- Android toybox did not finalize `screenrecord` through the previous `pkill -INT` path, leaving an `ftyp/free/mdat` file with no `moov` box;
- failed verifier commands and non-finalized recordings could still look like uploaded proof.

The branch moves emulator work into committed Bash processes, queues and drains early native deep links, exposes renderer readiness, acknowledges/replays CONNECT delivery within a bounded window, and ensures only the correct startup owner can claim a deep link. It also forces the emulator software-IME policy, polls the actual IME hierarchy, terminates `screenrecord` by PID with SIGINT, waits for encoder/transport exit, and rejects incomplete ISO-BMFF output.

# Final remote-loopback correction

The final hosted run exposed one more device-only ambiguity: the remote-mac harness deliberately forwards the host through `http://127.0.0.1:31337`, while the Android client previously treated every loopback-shaped URL as the bundled native agent. That hijacked the forwarded request and returned `local_agent_unavailable` even though the remote coordinator was healthy.

The exact head now resolves Android routing from persisted runtime mode, durable Cloud-session precedence, and build defaults before deciding whether loopback HTTP belongs to the native bridge. IPC remains unambiguously native. The mounted-App regression drives a real `CONNECT_EVENT` through deferred first-run adoption and asserts the observable `adopt → complete → retry` outcome sequence, remote mode, shell state, and success notice.

Final local gates: 10 changed UI test files pass 143/143; the enforced changed-file coverage gate remains above 50% for every executable target (81.05% mean for the final routing slice); test-realness reports zero regressions; and `bun run verify` passes 573/573 Turbo tasks plus all audits and 28/28 dist-path consumers.

# Review map

Start with:

1. `.github/workflows/android-device-e2e.yml` and `scripts/mobile/android-emulator-webview-ci.sh`;
2. `packages/app/src/mobile-lifecycle.ts`, `packages/ui/src/events/index.ts`, and `packages/ui/src/state/use-startup-shell-controller.ts`;
3. `packages/app/scripts/lib/android-capture.mjs` and `packages/app/scripts/android-assistant-verify.mjs`;
4. the exact-head Actions runs and downloaded artifacts linked below once complete.

# Verification

Exact head: `e44bd654f26`

- Exact changed-test lane: 29 Bun + 77 Vitest (106/106), including real command bytes, playable MP4 finalization, native delivery, and startup transitions.
- App scripts: prior branch-wide suite 500 Bun + 562 Vitest; all edited focused slices remain green.
- App/UI typechecks pass.
- Android debug Java compile: 484 tasks, success (excluding the unrelated missing `copyForkLlamaLib` artifact).
- Changed-file gate: all seven executable targets clear 50%; startup reducer 92.96%, startup ownership 90%, verifier library 99.54%, capture 75.19%, lifecycle 83.33%, verifier CLI 69.64%, events 57.89%; mean 81.22%.
- `bun run verify`: 573/573 Turbo tasks, all follow-on audits, and 28/28 dist-path consumers.
- Mandatory exact-head `bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app`: 246/246 passed; 0 broken and 0 needs-work verdicts after manual review.
- Final exact-head PR/device run: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29329810149
- Final exact-head full API-34 dispatch: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29329831684
- Final exact-head app aesthetic audit: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29329810125
- Replacement exact-head PR/device run: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29308643258
- Replacement exact-head full API-34 dispatch: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29308665988
- First diagnostic PR device run: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29304246350
- First diagnostic full API-34 dispatch: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29304250797

The diagnostic runs are intentionally retained: they prove the old shell failure was removed and expose the three exact device-level defects repaired by the final commit. They are not represented as passing acceptance evidence.

# Risk

Medium. This changes mobile lifecycle ordering and CI evidence acceptance, but replay is bounded, ownership is phase-typed, failed states remain failures, and the real hosted emulator lanes will run before the draft is promoted. No model or prompt behavior changes.

# Evidence Gate

<!-- evidence-row:before-screenshots -->
- [x] [Before: forwarded remote wrongly rendered Cloud sign-in](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/16320-before-cloud-onboarding.jpg)
<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- [x] N/A - there is no rendered design change; the required exact-head full app audit passed 246/246 views and was manually reviewed and its applicable mobile/desktop captures will be manually reviewed.
<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- [x] [Diagnostic API-34 run and its captured device bundle](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29304250797) show the pre-fix truncated recording; replacement exact-head MP4 proof is being collected.
<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->
- [x] [Diagnostic PR/device logs](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29304246350) and [full dispatch logs](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29304250797) identify startup acknowledgement, IME, and encoder-finalization failures; replacement exact-head logs are pending.
<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->
- [x] [Diagnostic WebView/Playwright run](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29304250797) proves native ingress reached the renderer but onboarding stayed on cloud sign-in; replacement exact-head state receipt is pending.
<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->
- [x] N/A - no agent, action, provider, prompt, model selection, or model output behavior changes.
<!-- evidence-row:domain-artifacts -->
- [x] [Diagnostic Android XML/JSON/screenshots/logcat/recording artifact](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29304250797) was downloaded and inspected; replacement exact-head artifact and digest are pending.

# Manual review of the diagnostic runs

The first hosted artifacts were downloaded and opened rather than inferred from job status. They showed:

- the cold deep link entered Capacitor but the app remained on cloud sign-in because restore cleared the acknowledged remote;
- assistant role/default IME were correct, while no software-IME mic was visible on the hardware-keyboard emulator;
- the pulled recording contained `ftyp`, `free`, and `mdat` but no `moov`, proving a non-empty file was not watchable evidence.

The final commit has direct regression coverage for each failure. Replacement device artifacts will be reviewed with the same standard.

# Known external gap

The full embedded Bun + llama LOCAL chat path is arm64-only. No repository runner currently exposes the required physical-device labels, so that row remains explicitly blocked rather than being inferred from the x86_64 emulator.

topPRs.title: fix(chat): make streaming persistence and telemetry exact
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Closes #17098

## Outcome

This makes chat streaming a single, observable provider → runtime → SSE → React → database pipeline and removes latency policy from correctness CI.

The runtime now has one owner for assistant-message persistence, the SSE completion frame carries the exact committed IDs, the client reconciles optimistic messages in place, and normal streaming performs no post-response history reload. Failed persistence emits an error and never a fake `done`.

## Runtime and persistence

- Return the exact response-memory IDs committed by `DefaultMessageService`.
- Reuse those IDs in the chat route instead of writing or reading the assistant response a second time.
- Preserve callback-before-persistence delivery for fast first response, with the same-room persistence barrier added upstream, while withholding SSE `done` until the write succeeds.
- Mark genuinely ephemeral responses explicitly; never invent a database ID.
- Treat delta streams as deltas. The previous overlap heuristic could corrupt `Fast streaming stays smooth.` into `Fastreaming staysmooth.`.
- Remove the hidden 30-second runtime-ready gate.
- Remove the implicit 180-second chat-generation abort, 60-second browser SSE idle abort, 60-second trajectory-finalization abort, and 5-second conversation-restore race. Cancellation is now caller-owned through `AbortSignal` unless a caller explicitly configures a boundary.
- Move trajectory persistence/finalization off the visible-response path while tracking it as post-delivery work.

## Providers, cache, and database

- Providers selected for a compose run execute concurrently through one `Promise.all`.
- Stage 1 excludes context it cannot consume; the planner reuses all already-composed provider results and refreshes only `RECENT_MESSAGES` when an early reply changed history.
- Replace mutable one-second identity/entity caches with exact turn-scoped promise memoization, rejection eviction, and explicit invalidation.
- Memoize sender-role, room, and related-entity reads within a turn.
- Skip attachment-history database work for ordinary text turns.
- Make SQL memory creation one atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`, removing the read-before-write race and extra database round trip.
- Cache only successful shared-agent scope authorization. Failed 401/403/404 hydration is never persisted, so a corrected credential, tier, or agent row is observed on the next authoritative attempt instead of serving a stale denial for 30 seconds.

## Browser behavior

- Reconcile optimistic user/assistant IDs in place from the completion frame.
- Do not reload conversation history after an ordinary successful response.
- Reload only when the response is action/incomplete or committed IDs are unavailable.
- Replace requestAnimationFrame token throttling—which can stop making progress in background tabs—with microtask burst coalescing and a synchronous terminal flush.
- Remove the reconnect debounce/speculative resend path; user-triggered resend starts immediately and remains explicit.
- Add the missing `rate_limited` SSE contract.

## CI and telemetry

- Replace the ~1,000-line latency workflow with a small, manual, observational workflow.
- Remove numeric latency acceptance thresholds, regression ratchets, production-code-changed/test-changed gates, and the workflow self-test enforcing those policies.
- Run direct and gateway observations concurrently and upload raw JSONL. Telemetry reports numbers; it does not decide correctness.
- Remove numeric enforcement from inference-auth latency tooling.
- Add a real browser telemetry harness using the production route, production stream client, `useChatSend`, React transcript, real HTTP/SSE, and PGLite.
- Expand the Cerebras runner to cover the complete production chat flow plus an explicit concurrent sweep of every registered provider.

## PR review

- #16882: closed unmerged. The proposed provider deadline would turn latency into missing context and make a slow dependency look healthy.
- #16820: closed unmerged. Browser telemetry is retained here, but the numeric merge gate and changed-production-requires-changed-test policy are removed.
- #17037: merged and retained. Dashboard replies have one transport owner.
- #17057: merged; its useful DB coalescing is retained, while this branch replaces mutable TTL-based identity/entity reuse with exact turn-scoped memoization.
- #17060: merged and retained. Cerebras strict object schemas remain recursively closed instead of being stripped.
- #17076: merged and retained as a cache-only shared inference hot path. This branch removes its remaining negative-scope TTL, which could serve stale denial after state was already corrected.

## Final live telemetry

Two consecutive final-base runs generated at 2026-07-23T22:00:03Z and
2026-07-23T22:03:19Z. Together they cover 60 live Cerebras
`gemma-4-31b` production turns.

### End-to-end chat

| Measure | p50 | p90 | p95 | max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full visible response | 396.114 ms | 799.086 ms | 869.371 ms | 2582.162 ms |
| First visible token | 389.000 ms | 773.000 ms | 817.000 ms | 2528.000 ms |
| LLM inference | 353.584 ms | 742.264 ms | 842.271 ms | 2564.000 ms |
| Provider composition | 8.222 ms | 25.000 ms | 32.198 ms | 141.000 ms |
| Message ingress | 2.000 ms | 4.545 ms | 7.000 ms | 95.849 ms |
| Message delivery | 3.000 ms | 5.000 ms | 7.000 ms | 57.000 ms |
| Message-service overhead | 4.042 ms | 14.736 ms | 21.162 ms | 149.989 ms |
| Background quiescence | 20.657 ms | 111.116 ms | 184.010 ms | 1040.171 ms |

- 60/60 turns succeeded and each made exactly one live LLM call.
- 1,440/1,440 provider executions completed with zero errors.
- Cerebras reported 92,416 cached input tokens out of 150,504 prompt tokens
  (61.4043%).
- Every distinct proof token was present in both the returned and streamed
  response.

The `50 ms` figure is not normal synchronous message-service overhead. Across
both runs the exclusive wrapper remainder is 4.0 ms at p50. The outlier run
contained one synchronized PGLite/storage stall: participant-state reached
91 ms, FACTS 55 ms, RECENT_MESSAGES 50 ms, and delivery persistence 57 ms in
the same turn. Another turn inflated many otherwise trivial providers together.
That shape proves process-wide database/event-loop scheduling, not serial
provider execution. The 149.989 ms wrapper outlier was a gap between compose
completion and stage-one preprocessing; it disappeared on the immediate repeat
(22 ms max), consistent with Bun GC/event-loop scheduling.

The remaining end-to-end outliers were model-side: the repeat had two Cerebras
calls at 2.1–2.56 seconds while local provider and delivery spans remained
normal. Detached message events, evaluators, and run-ended work occur after
terminal response visibility; they can still contend with local PGLite, but no
longer delay the visible response.

Normal production compose selected ten providers (60 calls/provider):

| Provider | p50 | p90 | p95 | max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FACTS | 8.000 | 24.625 | 32.248 | 141.228 |
| RECENT_MESSAGES | 4.463 | 7.657 | 18.198 | 107.292 |
| CHANNEL_TOPICS | 0.252 | 0.463 | 0.593 | 1.603 |

| ATTACHMENTS | 0.199 | 0.375 | 0.487 | 1.452 |

| REPLY_CONTEXT | 0.148 | 0.257 | 0.340 | 0.375 |
| PLATFORM_CHAT_CONTEXT | 0.094 | 0.185 | 0.212 | 0.235 |
| PLATFORM_USER_CONTEXT | 0.085 | 0.165 | 0.188 | 0.205 |

### Explicit all-provider concurrent sweep

The sweep deliberately bypasses final state reuse so every provider is actually
measured. Each row is 60 executions; 1,440/1,440 provider executions succeeded
with zero errors, aborts, or deadline failures.

| Provider | p50 | p90 | p95 | max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DOCUMENTS | 7.491 | 31.684 | 60.638 | 164.308 |
| ACTIONS | 3.632 | 25.288 | 40.220 | 157.934 |

| CHANNEL_TOPICS | 1.512 | 11.292 | 18.659 | 147.387 |
| CHARACTER | 1.337 | 13.989 | 18.499 | 147.294 |
| USER_EMOTION_SIGNAL | 1.240 | 13.974 | 18.356 | 101.909 |
| RUNTIME_MODEL_CONTEXT | 1.253 | 13.988 | 18.365 | 101.918 |
| UI_CONTEXT | 1.259 | 13.996 | 18.366 | 101.921 |
| CONTACTS | 1.092 | 8.499 | 14.924 | 101.764 |
| CURRENT_TIME | 1.086 | 8.493 | 14.922 | 101.740 |
| ATTACHMENTS | 1.056 | 8.467 | 14.859 | 101.748 |
| ACTION_STATE | 0.582 | 7.798 | 16.030 | 45.975 |
| PROVIDERS | 0.633 | 1.702 | 13.621 | 44.842 |
| RECENT_ERRORS | 0.579 | 1.342 | 13.594 | 44.815 |
| CONTEXT_BENCH | 0.555 | 1.204 | 13.574 | 44.797 |
| REPLY_CONTEXT | 0.540 | 1.178 | 13.566 | 44.788 |
| PLATFORM_CHAT_CONTEXT | 0.499 | 1.065 | 13.527 | 44.754 |
| PLATFORM_USER_CONTEXT | 0.494 | 1.058 | 13.522 | 44.751 |

Units are milliseconds. Synchronized inflation of cheap providers in the first
run produced the sweep tails. The immediate repeat normalized to
7.386/18.719/20.294 ms at p50/p95/max, confirming providers remain concurrent
rather than additive.

### Deliberately slow browser trace

With the model fixture emitting one token per second, visible server frames
arrived at 1089.23, 2091.32, 3093.43, and 4093.66 ms; browser DOM mutations
arrived at 1090.7, 2092.6, 3094.6, and 4137.5 ms. The completion frame reached
the browser at 4135.7 ms.

Provider output, reconstructed SSE text, completion text, React state, PGLite row, and rendered DOM were all exactly `Fast streaming stays smooth.`. The persisted assistant/user IDs exactly matched the completion frame. React committed seven times and performed zero history reloads.

## Verification

- `bun install`: clean lockfile/install.
- `bun run verify`: 578/578 tasks successful in 2m33s on the final rebased tree; all lint, typecheck, test-integrity, script/view inventory, and 28 dist-consumer checks passed.
- Latest readiness/streaming/persistence/recap semantic suite: 90/90 passed.
- Focused core/agent/UI streaming: 127 passed.
- Real conversation restore: 5 passed.
- Real PGLite memory integration: 38 passed.
- Shared scope, admission gate, and voice hot path: 68 passed.
- Real Miniflare Durable Object serialization: passed.
- Real browser telemetry: passed; screenshot generated and manually inspected.
- App visual audit: chat view good at all four desktop/mobile/rest/hover viewports with no chat render, overflow, or overlay defects.

## Evidence applicability

- Live model trajectory/log: represented by the 60 distinct proof-bearing turns and raw JSON reports produced by the runner.
- Database artifact: real PGLite user/assistant rows were read back and compared to the SSE completion IDs/text.
- Screenshot: generated and manually inspected locally; binary upload is N/A from the GitHub CLI-only environment.
- Video: N/A — this is transport/runtime behavior; the one-token-per-second trace records the full timing sequence numerically and the screenshot records final pixels.
- Live Eliza Cloud direct/gateway trace: N/A — this environment has Cerebras credentials but no Eliza Cloud, BitRouter, AI Gateway, or Cloudflare credentials. The local workerd/Miniflare and real PGLite paths were exercised instead.
